slot.brief: Find the equation of the tangent (or normal) to a curve at a given point, e.g. y² = 4ax or a hyperbola; ask for the line or its intercepts.

stem: The equation of the normal to the parabola $y^2=8x$ at $(2,4)$ is

verdicts.working: For y²=8x, implicit differentiation gives dy/dx=4/y=1 at (2,4). The normal has slope −1, so y−4=−(x−2), or x+y−6=0.

working:

$m_{\text{normal}}=-1$

Independent check: For y²=8x, implicit differentiation gives dy/dx=4/y=1 at (2,4). The normal has slope −1, so y−4=−(x−2), or x+y−6=0.
solution:
Differentiating $y^2=8x$ gives $2y\dfrac{dy}{dx}=8$, so the tangent slope at $(2,4)$ is $1$ and the normal slope is $-1$.
$$y-4=-(x-2)\Rightarrow x+y-6=0$$
